ruling.recommended_action: Send the case to a human reviewer: obtain the cancellation-side record (cancelled_by) for booking accepted 17:24:00 and cancelled 17:32:45, confirm which arrival event governs (platform arrival 17:27:05 vs driver tap 17:28:05), and hold the $6.61 charge pending review; do not execute a refund or affirm the fee on the current record.
ruling.reasoning:
The charge in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded at [F7] and [F4]. Under NS-0 the fee can only be charged through one of the enumerated branches: rider cancellation (NS-4 for an immediate booking) or a driver cancellation on a claimed rider no-show (NS-1/NS-2). Here the timeline records "cancelled by None" [F4], so the branch cannot be identified, and the trace marks NS-0 ✗ for that reason.

The driver's account that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited [F11] is met by system records on location and duration: the tap at 17:28:05 was 42 m from the pickup [F6], the vehicle was stationary 40 m from the pickup from 17:27:45 to the cancellation [F3], closest approach 4 m [F1], and the driver stayed within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap [F6] (5 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m [F2]). On those numbers alone NS-1 (i)–(iii) would appear satisfied, and even on the rider's most favourable reading the post-tap continuous in-radius wait of 4 min 40 s exceeds the default 3-minute threshold of NS-1(iii).

But NS-1 is only reachable through NS-0's driver-claims-no-show branch, and the record does not establish that this was a driver-side no-show cancellation rather than a rider-side cancellation: NS-4 and NS-1 cannot be told apart on [F4]. That is a missing record the clause needs, not an inference either side may win — under NS-1 (and the same requirement echoed in NS-2) the branch precondition must be recorded. The rider's app-glitch narrative (the booking "disappearing") is only a complaint narrative with no system support in [F4]–[F6], so it cannot itself defeat the fee; equally, the absence of the cancelled_by value cannot be read in the driver's favour.

Profile facts are not decisive: the rider's clean 90-day record [F15] and the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute [F16] cannot decide whether this fee stands under NS-1, and RD-6's account flag depends on the case being made out against the driver (which it is not), so no flag is warranted.

Because the record does not settle the branch element NS-0/NS-1 requires, the only consistent outcome is escalation: the $6.61 charge to be reviewed by a person against the cancellation-side record.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's own computation confirms the post-tap continuous in-radius wait of 4 min 40 s [F6], which is over the NS-1(iii) threshold rather than a ground for refund; the claim assists the driver, not the rider, and cannot support a refund under NS-1.

The 17:27:05 platform arrival log [F5] and the 17:28:05 driver tap [F6] do not change the outcome on NS-1's wait element (both exceed 3 minutes before the 17:32:45 cancellation [F4]); the real gap is the missing cancelled_by value [F4] under NS-0, not a contradiction that refunds the fee.

Consent under RD-5 concerns route deviation, not a no-show fee; NS-1 rests on arrival, location and continuous wait [F2][F3][F6], so the absence of rider agreement in the chat [F9][F10] does not by itself waive the fee.

Profile facts cannot decide a case: the rider's clean 90-day record [F15] and the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute [F16] do not establish or defeat the NS-1 elements; NS-1 turns on the system records of arrival and wait.

The alleged app glitch rests only on the complaint narrative with no system support in [F4]–[F6]; the record cannot confirm it, and NS-7 governs timing of fee disputes, not the escalation ground here (the gap is the missing cancelled_by value [F4]).

The rider's admission that both readings of the arrival anchor yield a wait over the threshold [F2][F6] concedes the NS-1(iii) element; it cannot ground refund_full, and the case turns on the unresolved NS-0 branch instead.

The driver cannot rest on both anchors at once: the 4 min 40 s post-tap wait [F6] and the 5 min 40 s cumulative wait [F2] are measured from different events, and NS-0's branch (driver-claims-no-show vs rider cancellation) remains unestablished on [F4].

The claim that the rider 'never made contact' is not established by the chat record: [F9][F10] show only one driver message with no rider message in evidence, and absence of a message is not proof of rider conduct; NS-1 turns on the driver's wait, not the rider's silence.

The premise that this is a rider-side no-show fails on [F4], which records cancelled_by = None; NS-0 permits the $6.61 only through the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4) or the driver-claims-no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2), and on this record neither is established.

The record cannot be said to be complete for decision: the decisive branch element cancelled_by is absent [F4] and the governing arrival event (17:27:05 [F5] vs 17:28:05 [F6]) is unresolved, so NS-1's precondition is not settled and NS-7/NS-0 route the fee dispute to human review rather than affirming the charge.
